}}'''Antonín Holý''' (1 September 1936 – 16 July 2012) was a Czech [[Medicinal chemistry|medicinal chemist]] known for his research on acyclic nucleoside phosphonates (ANPs), an important class of antiviral [[Nucleoside analogue|nucleotide analogues]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=De Clercq |first1=Erik |last2=Holý |first2=Antonín |year=2005 |title=Acyclic nucleoside phosphonates: a key class of antiviral drugs |journal=[[Nature Reviews Drug Discovery]] |volume=4 |issue=11 |pages=928–940 |doi=10.1038/nrd1877 |pmid=16264436}}</ref> He spent most of his scientific career at the [[Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry]] in Prague, where he served as director from 1994 to 2002.<ref>{{cite web |title=History |url=https://www.uochb.cz/en/history |access-date=19 August 2026 |publisher=[[Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry]]}}</ref> In a long-term collaboration with virologist [[Erik De Clercq]], Holý synthesized antiviral compounds including [[Cidofovir]], [[Adefovir]] and [[Tenofovir]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Watts |first=Geoff |date=15 September 2012 |title=Antonín Holý |journal=[[The Lancet]] |volume=380 |issue=9846 |page=970 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(12)61527-X}}</ref>

These compounds were subsequently developed into medicines used against [[Cytomegalovirus]] infections, [[Hepatitis B]] and [[HIV/AIDS]]. Tenofovir also became a component of combination therapies used for both HIV treatment and prevention.<ref>{{cite news |date=17 July 2012 |title=HIV drug creator Antonin Holy dies at 75 |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/lifestyle/science/hiv-drug-creator-antonin-holy-dies-at-75-idUSBRE86G0HY/ |access-date=19 August 2026 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> Holý's work has been credited with improving or extending the lives of millions of people with viral diseases worldwide.<ref>{{cite web |date=17 July 2012 |title=Groundbreaking chemist Antonín Holý dies at 75 |url=https://english.radio.cz/groundbreaking-chemist-antonin-holy-dies-75-8552713 |access-date=19 August 2026 |website=[[Radio Prague International]]}}</ref> Over his career, he co-authored around 600 scientific publications and held more than 60 patents.<ref>{{cite web |title=Antonín Holý |url=https://veda.upol.cz/en/awards-rankings/honorary-doctorates/antonin-holy/ |access-date=19 August 2026 |publisher=[[Palacký University Olomouc]]}}</ref>

==Scientific career==
Born in [[Prague]], [[Czechoslovakia]], Antonín Holý studied [[organic chemistry]] from 1954 to 1959 at the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics of [[Charles University in Prague]]. From 1960 he joined the [[Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry|Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry (IOCB)]] of the [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]] in Prague and had been a researcher there since 1963. He became the institute's lead scientist in 1967, and from 1983 headed its [[nucleic acids]] chemistry group. In 1987 he became head of the Bioorganic Chemistry Department and from 1994 to 2002 he was head of the IOCB.

Since 1976 he had collaborated on the development of new antiretroviral drugs with [[Erik De Clercq]] of the [[Rega Institute for Medical Research]] at the [[Katholieke Universiteit Leuven|Catholic University of Leuven]], [[Belgium]].<ref name="GileadIOCB">{{Cite web|url=https://new.gilead.com/news/press-releases/2006/7/gilead-sciences-and-the-institute-of-organic-chemistry-and-biochemistry-iocb-establish-new-academic-research-centre-in-prague-donation-by-gilead-honors-leadership-of-dr-antonin-holy-in-antiviral-drug-discovery-and-development|title=Gilead Sciences and the Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry (IOCB) Establish New Academic Research Centre in Prague; Donation by Gilead Honors Leadership of Dr. Antonin Holy in Antiviral Drug Discovery and Development|website=new.gilead.com|access-date=2020-01-08}}</ref>

His key contribution is the synthesis of [[nucleotide analogues]], synthetic mimetics of the building blocks of [[RNA]] and [[DNA]], that have found utility as inhibitors of viral replication. Clinically important compounds included [[Tenofovir]], [[Adefovir]] and [[Cidofovir]], which were subsequently developed into antiviral medicines.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Veda a umenia súvisia |url=https://legacy.blisty.cz/art/21096.html |access-date=2022-07-20 |website=legacy.blisty.cz |language=cs}}</ref> 

Tenofovir became an important component of combination therapies for HIV treatment and, in combination with [[Emtricitabine]], of [[Pre-exposure prophylaxis]] (PrEP) for HIV prevention.

In 2006, IOCB and [[Gilead Sciences]] launched the Gilead Sciences Research Centre, a five-year research partnership supporting work on human diseases at the institute.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gilead Sciences Research Centre |url=https://www.uochb.cz/en/gsrc |access-date=19 August 2026 |publisher=[[Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry]]}}</ref> Under the agreement, Gilead provided $1.1 million annually for five years to support the research programme.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Gilead Sciences and the Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry (IOCB) Establish New Academic Research Centre in Prague |date=13 July 2006 |publisher=[[Gilead Sciences]] |url=https://www.gilead.com/news/news-details/2006/gilead-sciences-and-the-institute-of-organic-chemistry-and-biochemistry-iocb-establish-new-academic-research-centre-in-prague-donation-by-gilead-honors-leadership-of-dr-antonin-holy-in-antiv |access-date=19 August 2026}}</ref>

Several antiviral drugs developed from this research were later approved for clinical use. [[Cidofovir]] (Vistide) was approved in the United States in 1996 for [[Cytomegalovirus retinitis]], followed by [[Tenofovir disoproxil]] (Viread) for [[HIV-1]] infection in 2001 and [[Adefovir|Adefovir dipivoxil]] (Hepsera) for chronic [[hepatitis B]] in 2002.<ref>{{cite web |date=26 October 2001 |title=Viread Approval |url=https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2001/21-356_Viread_Approv.pdf |access-date=18 August 2026 |publisher=[[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=20 September 2002 |title=Hepsera prescribing information |url=https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2002/21-449_Hepsera_prntlbl.pdf |access-date=18 August 2026 |publisher=[[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]]}}</ref> In 2004, [[Emtricitabine]] and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate were combined as [[Emtricitabine/tenofovir|Truvada]], which was approved for the treatment of HIV-1 infection.<ref>{{cite web |date=2 August 2004 |title=Truvada Approval |url=https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2004/021752s000_Truvada_Approv.pdf |access-date=18 August 2026 |publisher=[[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]]}}</ref>

==Death==
Holý retired on 1 September 2011, his 75th birthday, and died in Prague on 16 July 2012 following a long illness.<ref>{{cite news |date=17 July 2012 |title=Zemřel světoznámý chemik Antonín Holý, objevitel léků pro miliony lidí |url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/zemrel-chemik-antonin-holy.A120717_091737_domaci_jw |access-date=19 August 2026 |work=[[Mladá fronta DNES|iDNES.cz]]}}</ref> On the same day, the [[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]] approved [[Emtricitabine/tenofovir|Truvada]] for [[pre-exposure prophylaxis]] (PrEP) to reduce the risk of HIV infection.<ref>{{cite journal |last=De Clercq |first=Erik |year=2022 |title=The Elegance of the Acyclic Nucleoside Phosphonates (ANPs), Honoring Antonín Holý, Who Passed Away on 16 July 2012, at the 10th Anniversary of His Death |journal=Viruses |volume=14 |issue=9 |page=1978 |doi=10.3390/v14091978  |doi-access=free|pmc=9503179 |pmid=36146783}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=16 July 2012 |title=Truvada approval package |url=https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/021752Orig1s030Approv.pdf |access-date=19 August 2026 |publisher=[[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]]}}</ref>

* 1984 State Prize for Chemistry (''Acyklická analoga nukleosidů a nukleotidů'')<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2009-04-14 |title=UOCHB A.Holy |url=http://www.uochb.cas.cz/~nk/holy/holy.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090414111318/http://www.uochb.cas.cz/~nk/holy/holy.html |archive-date=2009-04-14  |access-date=2022-07-20 }}</ref>
* 1998 Honor plaque: Nucleic Acids Chemistry journal<ref name=":0" />
* 1999 Hanuš's Medal of the ''[[Czech Chemical Society]]<ref name=":0" />''; Honorary doctorate of the [[Palacký University, Olomouc|Palacký University]] in [[Olomouc]]<ref name=":0" />
* 2001 [[Descartes Prize]] of the European Union;<ref name="autogenerated3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.afi.cz/en/news/czech-chemistry-a-tradition-of-innovation-and-prosperity.html |title=Czech Chemistry: A Tradition of Innovation and Prosperity |accessdate=8 January 2009 |publisher=Association for Foreign Investment |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718163752/http://www.afi.cz/en/news/czech-chemistry-a-tradition-of-innovation-and-prosperity.html |archivedate=18 July 2011 }}</ref><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> The Medal of Merit of the Czech Republic (''Za zásluhy'') I. degree
* 2002 Elion Award of International Society for Antiviral Research;<ref name=":0" /> State Medal "''Pour merit''"<ref name=":0" />
* 2003 Honorary membership in the Rega Institute for Medical Research, Catholic University of Leuven, Belgium.
* 2004 Award ''Praemium Bohemiae'';<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://abicko.avcr.cz/cs/archiv/2005/2/obsah/praemium-bohemiae-podruhe.html |title=Praemium Bohemiae podruhé |accessdate=8 January 2009 |publisher=Academic Bulletin |date= |language=cs |archive-date=10 March 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090310113904/http://abicko.avcr.cz/cs/archiv/2005/2/obsah/praemium-bohemiae-podruhe.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Medal of the Czech Academy of Sciences: ''De scientia et humanitate optime meritis''
* 2005 Honorary doctorate of the [[Ghent University]] (Belgium); The Medal of Merit of the Faculty of Science at the Charles University in Prague.
* 2006 Member of the  [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]] ([[Salzburg]])
* 2006 Honorary doctorate of the [[Institute of Chemical Technology in Prague]]
* 2007 State Prize "Czech Head" (''Česká hlava'')
* 2008 Honorary Professorship at the [[School of Chemistry, University of Manchester]]
* 2009 Honorary doctorate of the [[University of South Bohemia in České Budějovice]]
* 2011 Silver memorial medal of the [[Senate of the Czech Republic|Senate of the Parliament of the Czech Republic]]
* 2012 Silver medal of the City of Prague
